record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: For continuous or Holder-continuous Lorentzian metrics, are length-maximizing timelike geodesics unique, what physical meaning would nonuniqueness of the timelike geodesic initial-value problem have, and should such nonuniqueness count as a spacetime singularity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a Lorentzian metric $g$ of low regularity — either continuous ($C^0$) or Hölder-continuous ($C^{0,\alpha}$ for some $0<\alpha<1$) — and assume that $(M,g)$ is time-oriented and globally hyperbolic so that, between causally related points $p \le q$, length-maximizing causal curves exist.

A locally Lipschitz curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is called timelike if its tangent vector is timelike almost everywhere, and length-maximizing between its endpoints if its Lorentzian length $L(\gamma)=\int_a^b \sqrt{-g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)}\,dt$ equals the time-separation $\tau(\gamma(a),\gamma(b))=\sup\{L(\sigma):\sigma\text{ future-directed causal from }\gamma(a)\text{ to }\gamma(b)\}$.

Address the following:

(a) For Lorentzian metrics $g$ of regularity $C^0$ or $C^{0,\alpha}$ ($0<\alpha<1$), determine whether the length-maximizing timelike geodesic between two chronologically related points $p\ll q$ is unique. That is, decide whether there can exist two distinct (up to reparametrization) length-maximizing future-directed timelike curves from $p$ to $q$, and characterize the regularity threshold at which uniqueness fails.

(b) Analogously, study the timelike geodesic initial-value problem: given a point $p\in M$ and a future-directed timelike vector $v\in T_pM$, decide whether there exists a unique inextendible locally length-maximizing timelike geodesic with initial data $(p,v)$ in the low-regularity setting.

(c) Provide a physical interpretation of nonuniqueness phenomena from (a) and (b) in the context of general relativity, and determine whether such nonuniqueness of geodesics (timelike worldlines of freely falling observers) should be regarded as a singularity of the spacetime $(M,g)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist. For globally hyperbolic continuous Lorentzian metrics, length-maximizing causal curves between causally related points are known to exist (Sämann and others). For metrics of Hölder class $C^{0,\alpha}$ or $C^{1,\alpha}$ with $\alpha<1$, solutions of the geodesic equation may fail to be local maximizers and the initial-value problem need not have unique solutions, so nonuniqueness phenomena are known to occur. However, a complete classification of uniqueness/nonuniqueness across all low-regularity classes, and the physical interpretation as singularities, remain active questions in low-regularity Lorentzian geometry and Lorentzian length space theory.

status_evidence.title: On geodesics in low regularity
status_evidence.snippet: For metrics of Hölder class C^{1,α} for α<1, the geodesic problem is solvable but not uniquely, and the relation to extremal curves is subtle.
status_evidence.claim: Nonuniqueness of geodesic solutions occurs in the Hölder regime.

status_evidence.title: New approaches to Lorentzian geometry and causality theory in low regularity
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of length-maximizers between causally related points for continuous globally hyperbolic Lorentzian metrics.
status_evidence.claim: Existence (but not uniqueness) of maximizers is established in the continuous setting.

status_evidence.title: Maximality and Cauchy developments for Lorentzian length spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on Lorentzian length spaces continues to investigate geodesic structure in low regularity.
status_evidence.claim: The problem area is actively researched but not fully resolved.
